blocks.text: Nidhara is an **npm workspaces monorepo** with three workspaces: a **NestJS 11** backend using **Prisma** and **PostgreSQL**, a **Next.js 16** frontend, and a **Docusaurus** documentation site. This case study covers the authentication and session foundation, which is the part built so far. The finance ledger and personal growth features are planned, not shipped.

rows: Stored credential data, hashed with Argon2
One record per session, holding the rotating refresh hash and CSRF verification state
Immutable log of LOGIN_SUCCESS, LOGIN_FAILED, LOGOUT, and REFRESH_ROTATED with IP and user-agent
Tracks failed logins and account security status
Time-bounded privilege escalation with a verified method (PASSWORD, RECOVERY_KEY, MFA)

items.text: On signin, the server issues a short-lived access token and an httpOnly refresh cookie, and stores a hash of the refresh token on a new `AuthSession`.
The client calls `/auth/refresh` with the cookie and its `csrfToken`.
The server verifies the refresh hash and the CSRF token against the session record.
On success, it issues a new access token and a new refresh token, and replaces the stored hash, so the old token cannot be used again.
A replayed token or a logout revokes the session, and a security event is recorded.

blocks.text: The project is at prototype stage. The backend exposes **5 endpoints** across 2 controllers and has one smoke-level test (`app.controller.spec.ts`). Passkey and security-question authentication, the sudo escalation endpoints, and all finance features are on the roadmap. The `SudoSession` and `UserAccountSecurityState` tables exist in the schema, but the flows that use them are not built yet.
